headline: ⏰ THE 1:30 AT 355 COMANCHE IS 45 MINUTES OUT — and the call that has to happen BEFORE it is to Cassie C., who wrote an offer on this house at the old price and still does not know the number came down. 🔍 Behind it, the Fieldstone inspection is locked for Thursday 11:15 with the combo already given out, and nineteen hours on neither the sellers nor the buyer's agent has been told in writing.

hotSignals.signal: Cassie C. at RE/MAX Advantage answered 'interested: Yes' and wrote "Writing up an offer!" on her form while calling $299,000 too high — that is the offer confirmed dead on Saturday morning, from a buyer who was never told the price came down to $295,000.
hotSignals.action: ⏰ CALL HER BEFORE 1:30 TODAY. There is a showing on this house this afternoon, and you want the agent who already wrote one offer to know the number moved before somebody else likes it, not after. Thank her for showing, tell her the number her client called too high is now $295,000, and ask what gets their buyer in the house. Quote $295,000 and nothing else. No email — a buyer's agent on a live listing is a call, not a message. ⚠️ Her written read has aged out of the 14-day window; the call task is live and the signal is carried here deliberately rather than dropped.

hotSignals.signal: Angela B. at Keller Williams Vestavia filed the listing's other 'interested: Yes', objecting only to the price at $299,000 and noting her buyer had seen another home she liked.
hotSignals.action: Call her — the price objection has already been answered by the reduction and she was never told. A week on, the cross-shopped house is either under contract or not, and one call settles it. Quote $295,000 only. ⏰ Her read ages out of the window in five days, so the written record of this yes is on a clock even though the call is not.

hotSignals.signal: Robert B. at RealtyCore asked at 2:35 Saturday whether Thursday worked for the inspection — and the inspector, Ron G., then reached you directly by text at 5:08. You answered at 5:30: Thursday 8/13, 11:15 AM, with the lockbox combo.
hotSignals.action: ✅ RESOLVED — the appointment is set. ⚠️ TWO LOOSE ENDS AND BOTH ARE YOURS. Your sellers have not been told that an inspector has their door code for Thursday, and there is no outbound to them anywhere since that text. And the buyer's agent — who asked the question in writing — still has nothing written back; the whole confirmation happened over text with a third party. One call to the sellers, one line to the agent.

hotSignals.signal: Mallory W. at ARC Realty filed the only unqualified 'interested: Yes / priced just right' this board has ever taken — her buyer wants to write and is short on down payment, nothing else.
hotSignals.action: The agent call is cleared. The open item is the seller decision behind it — authorize a concession or hold at list — and one call covers this seller's three files.

Neither was ever told it came down. ⏰ THE CASSIE CALL IS A MORNING CALL BECAUSE OF THE 1:30 — she is the one agent already on record wanting this house, and she should hear the new number before today's buyer walks it, not after. ⚠️ CASSIE'S READ HAS AGED OUT OF THE FOURTEEN-DAY WINDOW and no longer appears in the list above; the call task remains live and the signal is carried in Hot Signals deliberately, so it does not vanish just because the form got old. ⛔ QUOTE $295,000 AND NOTHING ELSE on both agent calls — across five written reads and one preview, not one agent has ever put a different number on paper. ⚠️ Worth knowing before you call: the price-improvement post went live on Facebook late Saturday night without passing approval. Ask him on the call; a single unanswered notice is not evidence of an unsigned document. 🆕 AND ONE FOUND THIS MORNING: your CRM has this listing marked EXPIRED while it is under contract with a Thursday inspection — a data problem, not a deal problem, but it stops feeding every downstream system.
